chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever performs hajj on behalf of a person, the two share until, when he completes the obligatory tawaf, the sharing is cut off. So whatever act occurs after that belongs to that pilgrim.

key_terms.إِنْسَانٍ: another person on whose behalf the rite is performed
key_terms.اشْتَرَكَا: the two shared in the act or reward
key_terms.الْحَاجِّ: the pilgrim who is performing the hajj
key_terms.انْقَطَعَتِ الشَّرِكَةُ: the sharing came to an end

ai.seo_question: When someone performs hajj on behalf of another, which acts are shared and when does that sharing end?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who performs hajj on behalf of another person. The proxy and the one represented share in the act up to the completion of the obligatory tawaf, after which subsequent acts belong to the performing pilgrim.
